prompts.cilia:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a journal-quality scientific mechanism schematic for a Research card on the author's academic homepage. User explicitly requests high similarity to the supplied figures from their own published article, rather than a loose artistic interpretation. The supplied page is a STRUCTURAL AND SCIENTIFIC reference. Preserve actual robot geometry, relationships and physical mechanism. Redraw selected schematic portions cleanly on pure white with muted gray devices, controlled blue/red/orange scientific color coding, crisp thin outlines, light non-photorealistic shaded technical solids. Wide landscape canvas about 1.65:1. Main content remains legible at 350px thumbnail width and lies inside a 7 percent safe margin. Match the sober graphical-abstract style of the paper. No photographic materials, glossy glass, glitter, droplets, cinematic lighting, decorative gold, exaggerated anatomy, invented robot features, charts, fabricated measured data, publisher logos, article paragraphs, page borders or page numbers. No copied microscopy panels. Only a handful of very short clean English labels where requested. This is a qualitative mechanism schematic.
Primary request: Redraw CiliaVine's real construction and flow-control principle from the reference FIGURE 1, focusing on panel B and the upper-right mechanism view in panel A. The reference page's middle-left panel B shows the critical structure: a very thin long medical guidewire, with short STRAIGHT FLAT NARROW RECTANGULAR magnetic PDMS strips attached in a spiral sequence around it. Make these strips like thin blunt-ended flexible slats, not broad pointed leaves, not curved flower petals, and not an auger. Roughly 10–15 strips protrude obliquely from a slender central wire over a long narrow active segment; maintain the paper's geometry and proportions, with no thick cylindrical machine casing and no mechanical connector housings. Show a clean three-quarter main view of this gray cilia array within a simplified open cutaway red/rose vessel. Use small white or blue directional flow arrows and a few blue tracer dots to communicate transverse transport and local recirculation as in Figure 1A. A modest thin double-headed arrow parallel to the guidewire labeled 'Magnetic actuation' indicates field-driven open/closed oscillation. A small technical inset on the left may show the same strips opened away from the wire and closed closely around it, labeled only 'Open' and 'Closed'. Favor real structure over filling the scene. Retain gray strips and guidewire as in the source rather than inventing teal biological leaves. Do not reproduce black microscope photographs, captions or text from the original page.

Primary request: Faithful redrawing of the magnetic water-strider robot's ACTUAL design in the supplied Figure 1 of Wang et al., Advanced Science 2023. The most important structural source is TOP-LEFT PANEL A; the physical mechanism source is MIDDLE-LEFT PANEL E. Preserve that real geometry: a tiny compact square/rectangular head at the TOP joins exactly FOUR very THIN long slender flexible legs that curve steeply downwards from the head, each ending in a short outward-curving bent foot. Each leg is narrow like the gray slender arms visible in panel A, roughly uniform width; do not render broad flat propeller blades, starfish paddles, a disc hub, rotor, or a four-point flat cross. Render the device in graphite gray as in the original paper, and include small red magnetization direction arrows along two visible legs, matching the source's meaningful mechanism. Main left half: a large clean oblique technical structure drawing very similar to panel A, centered above a pale cyan horizontal water-interface plane, four feet just touching the surface; tiny restrained surface dimples, no photographic ripples, reflections or splashes. A thin vertical blue arrow labeled only 'B' indicates applied magnetic field. Right half: a minimal three-state side-view sequence of this EXACT SAME structure, following panel E: a low splayed preload stance on the water, a rapid closing-leg take-off stance with bent foot contact, then an airborne upright stance with four thin legs hanging down. Use small pale blue connecting arrows and labels exactly 'Preload', 'Take-off', 'Flight'. The reference frames show a characteristic inverted-U/hairpin silhouette during flight; follow this, not a flat X silhouette. No experimentally measured times, heights, angles, axis plots, scale bars or numerical claims. Clean white journal-figure background, simple light cyan water line, sparse red/blue arrows, grayscale robot. Accurate mechanics and structural proportions matter more than artistic polish. Do not reproduce microscopy panels, plots, article headers, caption text, or journal branding from the source.
